evidence.observation: The plan says `gnd flatten MODEL --out DIR` "writes `<stem>.flat.orm.json` and `<stem>.flattening.json` into `DIR`", and IR2-C2 requires "`gnd check` verdicts over the written `checking.orm.flat.orm.json` equal those over `checking.orm.json` on `composed.population.json`". Context: src/gnd/examples/literature/interop_fixture/checking.orm.json declares reference_populations [{'id':'method-catalog','path':'reference/catalog.json',...}]. flatten_model (model/flattening.py:33-35) pops only includes and fact_type_constraints, so the flat model keeps that relative path. References are bound relative to the model file's directory (api.py:1165 `root=reference_root or Path(model_path).parent`), and only commands/judgments.py offers --reference-root. A flat model written to a DIR other than the root's directory therefore cannot bind its reference population under `gnd check`. Neither the IR2 contract nor IR2-C2 says where DIR must be or how references are carried. IR2-C2 is a (p1) sentence.

concerns.recommendation: In the IR2 contract, state what a flat model written outside the root's directory means for its relative reference_populations paths: require DIR to be the model's directory, refuse otherwise, or document that the reference files must be placed under DIR. Fix the directory IR2-C2 uses so its check parity can be tested.
concerns.title: gnd flatten --out DIR leaves the flat model's relative reference paths unresolvable outside the root's directory

evidence.observation: H7 and IR3-C1 name the flat files `extraction.flat.orm.json` and `checking.flat.orm.json`, but IR2-C2 (a (p1) sentence) names `checking.orm.flat.orm.json`. §2 IR2 says flatten uses "the names `gnd extract` uses (`extract/service.py:_flattening_names`)". Context: bundle_stem (extract/bundle.py:46-61) strips only the first matching suffix of (".orm.yaml", ".orm.yml", ".yaml", ".yml", ".json"), so `checking.orm.json` gives stem `checking.orm` and the file is `checking.orm.flat.orm.json`. H7's and IR3-C1's names do not match what IR2 will write.

concerns.recommendation: Use the stem-derived names (`checking.orm.flat.orm.json`, `extraction.orm.flat.orm.json`) throughout H7 and IR3-C1, or note that those names are probe-local, so the specs and docs cite the names `gnd flatten` actually writes.
concerns.title: Flat-model file names disagree between H7, IR3-C1 and IR2-C2

summary: r3 is sound. Each phase can be specified, implemented and tested as written. I re-read every cited location and all of them match this checkout: _includes.py:61-77 and :217-218, api.py:1157/1162/1163/1195-1198, judgments.py:470-471/507/569, emit.py:21/27-31/35-36/60-64, pyrel_rules.py:2415, commands/export.py:15-26, extract/service.py:191 and _flattening_names, projection.py:319, cli.py:650+, EXIT_COLLISION=11, and the schema's error.reason enum. Every named test and lane file exists. D4 is sufficient: parse_declarations requires a 64-hex sha256 on every include and compose refuses hash-mismatch, so the root sha256 checked at judgments.py:569 binds every include. R0.6 holds for each changed route because each change branches only on a root that declares includes. I found no blocking concern. Two non-blocking items remain: reference paths in a flat model written to another directory, and inconsistent flat-file names.
